briefs.headline: Neto scores twice as Chelsea win 2-0 at Everton
briefs.summary: Pedro Neto scored 44 seconds into the second half and in the 90th minute from Jordan Henderson's deflected free kick Saturday, ending Everton's unbeaten start; Mike Penders, 21, replaced the injured Emi Martinez for Chelsea's first league clean sheet in 23 matches.

briefs.headline: Martinez has surgery after head injury, says he will return in weeks
briefs.summary: The Chelsea goalkeeper collided with Jarrad Branthwaite in the 67th minute at Everton, was stretchered off receiving oxygen and posted from a hospital bed Saturday night that the operation went well and he would be back "in a few weeks"; Xabi Alonso called it "a concussion, but more than that."

briefs.headline: Isak's winner carries Liverpool past nine-man Brentford 2-1
briefs.summary: Keane Lewis-Potter headed Brentford ahead in the 44th minute before Yehor Yarmoliuk was sent off for a headbutt in first-half stoppage time; Victor Munoz equalised in the 62nd and Alexander Isak, back from injury, scored in the 70th. Szoboszlai and Frimpong went off hurt.

briefs.headline: Ravens expect Monken to want 'to kick our tail' in Cleveland reunion
briefs.summary: Cornerback Marlon Humphrey said the Browns coach, Baltimore's offensive coordinator the previous three seasons, will take Sunday personally whatever he says publicly; Cleveland hosts the Ravens at 1 p.m. ET with Tyler Huntley starting for the injured Lamar Jackson and first place in the AFC North at stake.

briefs.headline: Ohio beats Sacramento State 48-7 for a fourth straight win
briefs.summary: Duncan Brune ran for two touchdowns and Irving Brown for 87 yards and a score on eight carries Saturday night in Sacramento; Ohio led 27-0 at halftime, scored by quarter 7, 20, 14 and 7, and finished with 30 first downs and 469 yards.

briefs.headline: Hawkins throws for 464 as WVU beats Cincinnati 45-42 on a last-play kick
briefs.summary: Mike Hawkins Jr. completed 25 of 33 passes for a career-high 464 yards and three touchdowns and ran for two more Saturday in Morgantown; Jack Cassidy's 35-yard field goal as time ran out gave West Virginia its first lead of the day, a first Big 12 win and the end of a three-game losing streak.

briefs.headline: Rays beat Guardians 7-3 to even the ALCS at two games apiece
briefs.summary: Jonathan Aranda's seventh-inning single got under Chase DeLauter's glove in right for a two-run error that broke open a one-run game Saturday in Cleveland, and Yandy Diaz homered in the ninth; Tampa Bay scored in the third, sixth, seventh and ninth. Game 5 is 5 p.m. ET today on TBS, Parker Messick against Drew Rasmussen.

briefs.headline: Eagles place Hurts on injured reserve with blood clot
briefs.summary: Philadelphia announced the move Saturday after consulting outside doctors, sources told ESPN and NFL Network; the quarterback, sidelined indefinitely by a superficial clot in his calf, misses at least the Panthers, Cowboys, Commanders and Giants before the Week 10 bye.

briefs.headline: Bears plan to start Williams at Atlanta after three games out
briefs.summary: Caleb Williams, who tore a hamstring Sept. 20 against Minnesota, practiced fully all week and took the starter's reps, sources told NFL Network and ESPN on Saturday; Chicago is listed as questionable on him and went two and one in his absence.

briefs.headline: Auburn upsets No. 1 Georgia 27-24 on a field goal as time expires
briefs.summary: Alex McPherson's 34-yarder Saturday in Athens followed Gunner Stockton's fumble with 58 seconds left as Georgia drove for a go-ahead kick; Byrum Brown ran for 115 yards, and the AP No. 1 team lost in consecutive weeks for the first time since October 1990.

briefs.headline: BYU holds off No. 2 Notre Dame 28-24; Big 12 admits clock error
briefs.summary: Bear Bachmeier's 6-yard pass to Walker Lyons with 1:47 left put No. 8 BYU ahead Saturday in Provo and CJ Carr's last pass fell incomplete from the 9; the Big 12 said afterward one second should have gone back on the clock for one more Irish play. Five of the AP top eight lost on one day for the first time.

briefs.headline: Tennessee beats No. 6 Alabama 26-10 as the Tide lose a second straight
briefs.summary: DeSean Bishop ran for 159 yards and two touchdowns Saturday in Knoxville while Alabama managed 201 yards, turned the ball over four times and converted 2 of 13 third downs; the Crimson Tide dropped consecutive regular-season games for the first time since 2007.

briefs.headline: Verhaeghe and Bennett hat tricks lift Panthers over Kraken 8-3
briefs.summary: Carter Verhaeghe's natural hat trick Saturday in Sunrise made Florida the first NHL team with natural hat tricks in three straight games, after Brady Tkachuk's two; Sam Bennett scored his first three goals of the season and Matthew Tkachuk had three assists.

briefs.headline: Flyers beat Senators 3-1 for their first win after a record nine losses
briefs.summary: Porter Martone tied it and Matvei Michkov scored his 50th career goal on a power play Saturday in Philadelphia, ending a franchise-record season-opening skid; Linus Ullmark lost for the first time after six straight wins to start the year.

briefs.headline: McDavid has two goals and three assists as Oilers rout Mammoth 6-2
briefs.summary: Connor McDavid scored 40 seconds in Saturday in Salt Lake City and Edmonton led by five midway through the second period, splitting the home-and-home after Utah's win Thursday; Leon Draisaitl and Zach Hyman also scored and Tristan Jarry made 26 saves.

briefs.headline: No. 1 pick Dybantsa sprains ankle in Wizards' preseason finale
briefs.summary: AJ Dybantsa landed awkwardly on his left ankle after a jump shot Friday and limped off after 12 points in 15 minutes; coach Brian Keefe called it a mild sprain and holding him out precautionary. Washington opens the season Wednesday against Milwaukee.

briefs.headline: JSA stages Bangkok announcement for its first Thailand performance
briefs.summary: Takasaki oyakata (elder) said Saturday at a chanko festival in Tokyo's Roppongi that the June 11 to 13, 2027, performances at One Bangkok Forum mark 140 years of Japan-Thailand relations, a third straight overseas tour after London and Paris; Namatame, a juryo (second-division) wrestler whose mother is Thai, said he aims to reach makuuchi (top division) by then. The Kyushu basho (tournament) opens Nov. 8 in Fukuoka, 21 days out.

prime.item: Day 4. Proclamation SF-1-2026, signed Oct. 2 at 3:10 p.m. by Division of Marine Fisheries interim director Michael S. Loeffler and re-opened this morning at 5:53 a.m. by its files.nc.gov address, made the hand harvest of oysters from public bottom in internal coastal fishing waters effective at sunrise Thursday, Oct. 15, and says the season closes March 31, 2027, under Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 03K .0201 unless closed sooner by proclamation. The recreational limit it sets is one bushel per person per day, not to exceed two bushels per vessel per day, from public bottom; it is unlawful to possess oysters under three inches shell length, to possess commercial and recreational limits aboard the same vessel, or to take them from the oyster sanctuaries designated in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117. The division's proclamations index, all six pages read at 5:53 a.m., lists SF-1-2026 as issued Oct. 2 and effective at sunrise Oct. 15; NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened at 5:52 a.m. and still dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, reads oysters as season closed, unlawful to possess, and the proclamation is the later document. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries.

NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:52 a.m. with a browser user agent and dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, lists red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length and one per day, under federal red drum management; the division's flounder proclamation FF-27-2026, which the page links and which was re-read this morning with pdftotext, cites Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 3I .0124 requiring recreational anglers to report red drum, spotted seatrout, flounder, striped bass and weakfish harvest to the division. The proclamations index, all six pages read at 5:53 a.m., carries no 2026 recreational red drum proclamation. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries, and the limits page says a Coastal Recreational Fishing License is required in coastal waters, a separate license from the inland one. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 17 days old, has red drum as the main inshore target around Topsail.

prime.dates: Open; 14- to 20-inch slot, one over 26 inches
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists spotted seatrout, the speckled trout, at a 14- to 20-inch total-length slot with one fish over 26 inches allowed, three per day, no federal regulation. The division's proclamations index, read at 5:53 a.m., lists the harvest opening as FF-31-2026, issued June 25 and effective 12:01 a.m. July 1, 2026, and carries no later seatrout proclamation; the October proclamations on the index are the oyster opening, three commercial flounder orders (FF-42, FF-43 and FF-44-2026), a striped bass order and four gill net and stop net orders. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 17 days old, has the trout scattered, a few on early topwater, the guides waiting on cooler water; Beaufort's thermometer read 69.4 degrees this morning, down 7.6 from Saturday.

prime.species: Spanish mackerel, king mackerel and bluefish
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists Spanish mackerel at 12 inches fork length and 15 per day, king mackerel at 24 inches fork length and three per day, and bluefish with no minimum size and five per day, all under federal management plans. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 17 days old, has Spanish and bluefish plentiful from the surf and piers and kings to 32 pounds at Jolly Roger Pier.

NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists black drum at a 14-inch minimum and 25-inch maximum total length, 10 per day, sheepshead at 14 inches total length, five per day, neither under federal regulation, and spot with no minimum size and 50 per day under federal spot management. The reference calendar lists October as the peak of the spot run; the Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 17 days old, has black drum of three to four pounds at the bridges and oyster reefs, spot in the evening bottom-fishing catch at Surf City Pier and sheepshead in the Seaview Pier bottom catch.

Stay on the bank.", and the band is right: the fetcher's blown-out line is 500 cfs and the river is 87 above it. The recession paused Saturday: 638 cfs from 7 to 10 a.m., then a rise to 644 at 11, 649 at noon, 660 at 3 p.m., 676 at 5 p.m., 671 at 6, 676 at 7, 671 at 8, 665 at 9, 660 at 10, 644 at 11, 633 at midnight, 628 at 1 a.m., 607 at 2, 602 at 3, 597 at 4, 592 at 4:30 and 587 cfs at 5 and 5:15 a.m., the last point on the trace and the window low; stage went 3.19 Saturday morning to 3.26 at 5 and 7 p.m. and back to 3.09 at 5 a.m. The window high is 1,000 cfs and 3.79 feet at midnight Friday, the first point of this desk's window. The river is still 229 cfs above the 358 cfs it bottomed at Wednesday evening before Thursday's rise, cited from Friday's edition. The Gauley near Craigsville (03189100), above Summersville Lake, read 2,310 cfs and 12.75 feet at 4:30 a.m., the last point on its trace, against 2,530 cfs and 12.88 feet at 4:30 a.m. Saturday, the true 24-hour mark, down 220 on the day, and held 2,380 to 2,390 cfs from noon Saturday to 1 a.m. before easing. 03189600 below Summersville Dam, stage only, its discharge series again carrying no values, an eighth day, held 10.96 to 11.02 feet for the whole 24 hours, 10.99 at 4:45 a.m., with the window high 11.02 at 9:30 a.m. Saturday: Friday evening's restoration, 1.8 feet above the three previous nights, ran flat all day Saturday, a reading off a USGS stage trace and not a Corps statement; the Corps' Huntington District site was not opened and no release figure is printed. waters.working: Down a tenth on the day, and the fetcher's steady flag is right either way. The trace, pulled at 5:50 a.m., runs 25.15 at 5 a.m. Saturday, the true 24-hour mark and Saturday's edition reading, then 25.20 at 6, 25.11 at 7, 25.06 at 8, 25.02 at 9, 24.99 at 10, 24.93 at 11, 24.91 at noon, 24.84 at 1 p.m., 24.86 at 2, 24.83 at 3, 24.79 at 4, the day's low, 24.87 at 5, 24.94 at 6, 25.02 at 7, 25.11 at 8, 25.17 at 9, 25.19 at 10, the day's high, 25.18 at 11 and midnight, 25.17 at 1 a.m., 25.12 at 2, 25.10 at 3, 25.06 at 4, 25.05 at 4:45 and 25.05 at 5 a.m. That is down 0.10 on the day and down 0.14 from the 10 p.m. high; the fetcher's 24.97 is the first point of its own two-day window, the 5:45 a.m. Friday reading, not 24 hours ago, and against it the pool reads 0.08 up, inside the fetcher's steady band, so the flag holds on both counts. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 25.1 the gauge is in that band, with the up-and-pushing line at 27 feet. The window high is 25.29 at midnight Friday, the first point; the window low a single 15-minute point of 24.49 at 1:45 p.m. Friday. Thursday's Kanawha water is largely through: the Gauley near Craigsville read 2,310 cfs at 4:30 a.m. against 2,530 a day earlier, the Williams at Dyer went 638 to 587, and 03189600 below Summersville Dam, stage only, held 10.96 to 11.02 feet all day Saturday after Friday evening's restoration, readings of USGS traces and not Corps statements, the Corps' Huntington District site not opened, so no lake elevation and no Corps release figure is printed; what reaches Point Pleasant and when is the Corps' call and is not predicted here. At 25.1 on a normal pool the river fishes the structure itself: shad are the forage and skipjack are with them, so a white or pearl swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked down the current face of each wing dam and along the riprap where the current breaks, a half-ounce blade bait or a jigging spoon on the lock wall's deep edge for the sauger, crawfish-colored jigs in the rock for the smallmouth, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the outside bends for the blues and flatheads after dark, a first-quarter moon setting around midnight. NWS Charleston's Freeze Warning, updated 3:26 a.m., covers Mason County to 9 a.m. today; no other product covers the county at 5:51 a.m.

The trace, pulled at 5:50 a.m., runs 27.12 at 5 a.m. Saturday, the true 24-hour mark and Saturday's edition reading, then 27.20 at 6, 27.22 at 7, 27.25 at 8, 27.23 at 9 and 10, 27.39 at 11, the day's high, 27.24 at noon, 27.29 at 1 p.m., 27.27 at 2, 27.29 at 3, 27.22 at 4, 27.16 at 5, 27.21 at 6 and 7, 27.09 at 8, 27.17 at 9, 27.05 at 10, the day's low, 27.15 at 11, 27.16 at midnight and 1 a.m., 27.15 at 2, 27.25 at 3 and 4, 27.26 at 4:30 and 4:45 and 27.27 at 5 a.m. That is up 0.15 on the day and up 0.11 since 2 a.m.; the fetcher's 27.76 is the first point of its own two-day window, the 5:45 a.m. Friday reading, not 24 hours ago, and against it the gauge reads 0.49 down, which is where the falling flag comes from. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, up and pushing, expect colour and current, fish the slack behind anything solid, and at 27.3 the gauge is 0.27 above the 27-foot line between that band and normal pool, having spent all of Saturday above it after dipping to 26.89 at 12:30 a.m. Saturday, the window low; the window high is 27.82 at 4:30 a.m. Friday. Friday's rise was Thursday's Kanawha water passing; the gauge has held a 0.34-foot band, 27.05 to 27.39, for 24 hours, and what is above is easing: the Gauley near Craigsville 2,310 cfs at 4:30 a.m. against 2,530 a day earlier, the Williams at Dyer 638 to 587; 03189600 below Summersville Dam, stage only, held 10.96 to 11.02 feet all day Saturday after Friday evening's restoration, readings of USGS traces and not Corps statements. The Craigsville water is above Summersville Lake, which sits between it and this gauge; what the lake passes is the Corps' call and is not predicted here. At 27.3, the bottom of the up-and-pushing band and a tenth and a half higher than Saturday, the fetcher's own line is still the lure problem: the forage is shad and skipjack with crawfish in the riprap, so a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon swum through the eddy below each wing dam where the pushed water slacks, a half-ounce blade bait or a chartreuse-and-white paddletail on a half-ounce head held in the seam behind the riprap points in low light, a black-and-blue jig for the smallmouth and the drum in the slack pockets of the rock, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the slack of the outside bends for the blues and the flatheads after dark, a first-quarter moon setting around midnight; the lock wall fishes from the downstream side on a live skipjack for the hybrids when the gates open. NWS Charleston's Freeze Warning, updated 3:26 a.m., covers Cabell and Wayne counties to 9 a.m. today; no other product covers them at 5:51 a.m.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: high 2:08 AM at 3.1 ft, low 8:14 AM at 1.0 ft, high 2:42 PM at 3.9 ft, low 9:13 PM at 1.3 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: high 1:11 AM at 3.3 ft, low 6:56 AM at 1.3 ft, high 1:47 PM at 4.4 ft, low 8:27 PM at 1.4 ft. Water 69.4F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon first quarter, 46% lit, 7.0 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 2:08 AM and 2:42 PM in the sound.
waters.working: First quarter today: the fetcher's file carries the moon as first quarter, 46 percent lit and 7.0 days old, and the U.S. Naval Observatory's phase table, which answered at 5:53 a.m., puts the quarter at 16:12 UT, 12:12 p.m. ET today, the full moon at 04:12 UT Oct. 26 and the last quarter at 20:28 UT Nov. 1, so this is the bottom of the neap: the smallest swings of the fortnight, the gentlest current through the inlet and the least bait moving on the tide, with the springs building toward next Monday's full moon. The surf's midday high has come down from 5.3 feet a week ago Monday through 4.5 Saturday to 4.4 today, and the sound's 3.9 holds, the earlier figures cited from the week's editions. NWS Wilmington has two products on the water this morning. On the beach, a Beach Hazards Statement for Coastal Pender County (NCZ106), issued 3 a.m. today for 6 a.m. through 8 p.m. Sunday: a strong north-to-south longshore current and a moderate risk of rip currents for Pender County, which the Service says can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip currents, piers and jetties and off their feet; it is the first product on Coastal Pender in a week, after six quiet beach mornings. Off the beach, the Gale Warning for the coastal waters from Surf City to Cape Fear out 20 nautical miles (AMZ250), the marine zone off the beach and the inlet, re-issued at 2:26 a.m. today: north winds 25 to 30 knots with gusts to 40 and seas 7 to 10 feet until 8 a.m. Monday, hazardous seas that could capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility. Saturday's issue read 25 to 35 knots, seas 6 to 9 feet and an end at 11 a.m. Monday; the wind came down five knots at the top, the seas went up a foot and the end moved three hours earlier. It is a marine product for the ocean out 20 miles, not a sound product. All four sound events fall inside Sunday this morning and none carries a spillover tag: the sound at Hampstead topped out at 3.1 feet at 2:08 a.m., is in the last two hours of its ebb at press time, bottoming at a 1.0-foot low at 8:14 a.m., then fills 2.9 feet to a 3.9-foot high at 2:42 p.m. and drains 2.6 feet to a 1.3-foot low at 9:13 p.m.; the last two hours of that ebb, about 7:15 to 9:13 p.m., run into the dark, with sunset just before 6:30. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: high 1:11 a.m. at 3.3, low 6:56 a.m. at 1.3, high 1:47 p.m. at 4.4 and low 8:27 p.m. at 1.4, a 3.1- and 3.0-foot swing against Saturday's 3.3 and 3.1. Today's lags from the two tables are 57 and 55 minutes on the highs and 78 and 46 minutes on the lows; the morning low again lags longest, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, which stretches the drum window at the crew's spot past what a flat hour's offset would give. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 69.4 degrees at 5:30 a.m., down 7.6 from Saturday's 77.0 and the first reading under 70 this fall in this paper, the morning after the north wind came up; the fetcher's file gives no reading at Topsail itself. What is running is 17 days old, not a month: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report posted Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, and the feed carried it as its newest item at 5:51 this morning. East Coast Sports has slot red drum with over-slots mixed in off the surf and piers, Spanish and bluefish plentiful, kings showing more at the piers, trolled spoons working off the beach, and inshore red drum as the main target with no word on trout yet; Native Son has mullet everywhere and reds at the docks, creek mouths and grass lines, trout scattered, glass minnows thick off the beach and the kings still in 50 to 60 feet; Spring Tide has the reds schooled in the bays at 22 to 28 inches and better, topwater and artificials some days and cut bait others, trout quiet until the water cools, Spanish pushing inside the inlet on the high tide; Speckled Specialist has Carolina-rigged live mullet the best red drum bait, trout early on topwater and then live shrimp under slip corks in 15 to 20 feet, black drum of three to four pounds at the bridges and oyster reefs; Carolina Flats has big mullet moving into the ICW and the bigger reds on live finger mullet or artificials under popping corks, flounder as bycatch, false albacore due on the nearshore structure; Plan 9 has Spanish of 14 to 22 inches and false albacore just outside the inlet in 15 to 20 feet on small jigs; South End has the bigger Spanish in 45 to 50 feet over hard bottom under feeding birds and kings in the 8- to 12-mile range. The piers: Jolly Roger reports bait thick, multiple kings to 32 pounds, Spanish ramping up, and night bottom fishing producing red drum to 31 inches, Virginia mullet, pompano, bluefish, black drum and some flounder; Surf City Pier has good-sized Spanish on Gotcha plugs, slot and occasional over-slot reds, and evening bottom fishing with black drum, mullet, spot and croaker; Seaview Pier has the mullet migration starting, Spanish and bluefish on Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs, and a bottom mixed bag of flounder, sea mullet, spot, sheepshead, trout, black drum and the odd red. The reference calendar's October pattern, spot at peak, red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum, matches the report. On today's tides and this water, a tide problem before it is a lure problem, and a wind problem before either: the Gale Warning's north wind is on the ocean, and in the sound a north wind blows down the ICW and holds water out of the creeks on the ebb and lays the lee on the mainland shore. The sound is on the last two hours of its morning ebb until 8:14 a.m., the red drum stage, finger mullet the forage the file records and the report says the mullet are in, so a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig or a three-inch Gulp shrimp under a popping cork fan-cast a couple of feet off the channel edge where the creek mouths drain the grass, and a cut mullet chunk on the bottom at the same edge as the water gets low, from the lee bank. The flood from 8:14 a.m. to 2:42 p.m. covers the oyster bars and grass edges, mud minnows and shrimp the forage there, so a quarter-ounce gold spoon or a paddletail on a three-sixteenths-ounce head along the grass edges and across the oyster bars as they go under, and a live shrimp on a slip cork at the oyster bars and the bridge pilings for the black drum and sheepshead, the report's three- to four-pounders. The 2:42 p.m. high puts 3.9 feet of water over the grass and up the dock pilings, where the reds go on a flooded high, so a topwater walked over the grass edges and down the dock lines on the last of the flood, about 12:45 to 2:42 p.m., then a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig as the ebb starts. The red drum window proper is the bottom of the afternoon ebb, roughly 7:15 to 9:13 p.m., 53 minutes later than Saturday's and into the dark, the same Carolina-rigged mullet and cut mullet at the channel edges, with a 7.6-degree drop at Beaufort overnight the kind of cool-down the guides in the report say the trout are waiting on: a live shrimp under a slip cork in the deeper holes, 15 to 20 feet, on the first of the ebb, and the dock lights after the 9:13 p.m. low with the half moon down by midnight. Oysters are in their fourth day open under SF-1-2026 on the public bottom; the oyster bars the crew fishes over are the same structure, and the sanctuaries in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117 are closed to harvest. The surf side is under both products: the Beach Hazards Statement's longshore current and moderate rip risk from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. and the Gale Warning's 25 to 30 knots of north wind and 7 to 10 feet of sea on the water out 20 miles through Monday morning; the piers' Gotcha-plug Spanish bite on the flood to the 1:47 p.m. high, 4.4 feet at the pier, and the evening cut-bait session for slot reds both fall inside them. Slack at 8:14 a.m., 2:42 p.m. and 9:13 p.m. is dead water. Flounder are release only.
